headline: AYA GOLD SMASHES OWN RECORD — 890 g/t AgEq Over 51.5m in Morocco Blows Out Resource Shell
snippet: Aya Gold & Silver (TSX: AYA) reported its strongest-ever Boumadine intercept: 890 g/t silver equivalent over 51.5 metres, including 1,504 g/t AgEq over 19.3 metres — 70 metres below the current resource pit shell. Year-to-date the company has drilled 69,209 metres at Boumadine with 11 active rigs and a 360,000-metre program planned through 2027.

headline: GOLD BUYERS STEP IN AT $4,469 — Week-Long Slide Halted as Central Banks Buy the Dip
snippet: Gold recovered to $4,469–$4,499 on May 20 after a week-long selloff drove the metal to its lowest close since March 30. Physical buyers stepped in at support while the People's Bank of China confirmed an 8-tonne reserve addition in April — its largest single-month purchase in 15 months — signalling that central bank demand intensifies into price weakness.

headline: BEST EVER: GR Silver Hits 45.1m at 1,623 g/t Silver in Mexico, Core Runs 8,579 g/t
snippet: GR Silver Mining (TSXV: GRSL) released what it calls its best-ever drill results at San Marcial on the Plomosas Project in Mexico: hole SMS26-04 returned 45.1 metres grading 1,623 g/t Ag, including an 8.25-metre core at 8,579 g/t Ag. The intercept sits in the SE Extension and highlights resource growth potential between the Central Area and SE Extension.

headline: Troilus West Rim Drills OUTSIDE the Resource — Analysts Flag M&A Target at 2.92 g/t AuEQ
snippet: Troilus Mining (TSX: TLG) extended its West Rim Zone at the copper-gold Troilus Project in northern Quebec with 2.92 g/t AuEq over 19 metres — entirely outside the current resource estimate and within 200 metres of the planned pit. Northern Miner analysts noted the intercepts underscore acquisition potential, with all West Rim holes remaining open in multiple directions.

headline: CHILE UPGRADES COPPER FORECAST to $5.55/lb — Tight Supply and EV Demand Underpin Record Outlook
snippet: Chile's state copper commission Cochilco raised its 2026 average copper price forecast to $5.55 per pound in its Q1 market trends report, citing firm demand from EVs, AI data centres, and grid electrification alongside constrained mine supply. The commission sees 2027 prices holding elevated at $5.10/lb and forecasts global refined copper demand rising 1.5% to 28.2 million tonnes in 2026.

headline: Ghana FORCES MINERS to Sell 30% of Output to Central Bank as Africa Stockpiles Gold
snippet: Ghana is requiring large-scale gold miners to sell 30% of their annual output to the Bank of Ghana — up from 20% — as the country aims to grow reserves that stood at 19.2 tonnes as of February 2026. The move mirrors similar policies across other African producers and reflects accelerating dedollarisation by emerging-market central banks, which collectively bought close to 1,000 tonnes of gold in 2025.

headline: SIXTH STRAIGHT YEAR: Silver Demand Exceeds Supply as Industrial Deficit Shows No End
snippet: Silver enters a sixth consecutive year of structural supply deficit, with industrial demand from solar manufacturing, EVs, and electronics continuing to outpace mine production. China alone imported over 790 tonnes of silver in early 2026, while investment demand added 13.5 million ounces year-over-year — a combination that keeps the supply math tilted against new production catching up.

headline: IRAN CEASEFIRE LIFTS COPPER, But Smelter Margin Collapse Signals Tighter Supply Ahead
snippet: The US-Iran ceasefire struck in April 2026 removed Strait of Hormuz supply fears and lifted copper back above US$6/lb, but a separate alarm is building: smelter treatment charges have collapsed to record lows as concentrate tightens. Crux Investor argues this structural squeeze in refined copper supply could accelerate into H2 2026 regardless of demand-side volatility.

headline: MP Materials Posts 117% NDPR SALES SURGE, Breaks Ground on Pentagon-Backed Magnet Plant
snippet: MP Materials (NYSE: MP) posted Q1 2026 revenue of $132.9 million — up 49% year-over-year — on record NdPr sales of 1,006 metric tonnes, a 117% annual increase. The company broke ground on its DoD-backed 10X Magnetics facility in Texas, backed by $400 million in Pentagon equity and a 10-year offtake agreement, with initial magnet revenue targeted for H2 2026.

headline: SURPLUS TO DEFICIT: Morgan Stanley's 80,000-Tonne Lithium Warning as Energy Storage Booms
snippet: Morgan Stanley is forecasting an 80,000-tonne lithium carbonate equivalent deficit in 2026 — a dramatic reversal from an expected 61,000-tonne surplus in 2025. The catalyst: grid-scale battery storage demand driven by China's power sector reforms is projected to account for 31% of total lithium consumption in 2026, up from 23%, eating into the EV-dominated demand mix.

headline: RARE EARTHS CORRECT — NdPr Falls 21% in April But Still 88% Higher Year-to-Date
snippet: NdPr oxide fell 21% in April to $99.61/kg — the sharpest monthly pullback since the Q1 rally — but remains 88% above January's opening price of ~$53/kg. Analysts expect consolidation between $95–$115/kg through Q2 as inventories adjust, with China's export controls and the $12 billion US Project Vault strategic reserve program providing a structural price floor.

headline: LEVERAGE UNLOCKED: Why Gold Miners Are Poised to Outrun the Metal at $4,500 Gold
snippet: With gold holding above $4,500 and industry AISC averaging below $2,000 per ounce, producers are generating record free cash flow margins. Multiple institutional analysts argue miner equities remain undervalued relative to bullion — Agnico Eagle posted a realized gold price of $4,861/oz in Q1 at an AISC of $1,483 — and that operating leverage will drive equity outperformance as valuations catch up to fundamentals.
